data.title: Hydrogen peroxide (1.5–6%)
data.category: More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antibacterials & antiseptics_

**Class:** Oxidising antiseptic

## Mechanism of action
- Releases oxygen on contact with tissue catalase → effervescence loosens debris; weak antibacterial (especially anaerobes)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Cleansing of dirty wounds and crusts, ear wax; 40% solution for seborrhoeic keratoses (approved USA); cream 1% for impetigo (Europe)

## Dose & formulations
- 3% for cleansing (diluted); short contact

## Adverse effects
- Delays healing (toxic to fibroblasts) with repeated use; gas embolism if used in closed cavities under pressure; bleaching of hair and skin (transient white blanching)

## Contraindications
- Closed body cavities, deep wounds under pressure

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Effervescence from catalase; harmful to granulation tissue with repeated use

_Sources: Khopkar ch.30 (Hydrogen peroxide). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
